newsitem.title: USA: American Express record income fueled by financial unit.
newsitem.headline: American Express record income fueled by financial unit.

text.p: American Express Co. Thursday reported record first-quarter profits, fuelled by a 21 percent increase in earnings at the company's American Express Financial Advisors unit.
Net income rose to $454 million, or 94 cents, in the quarter from $396 million, or 80 cents a share, a year ago. Revenues grew to $4.2 billion from $3.9 billion.

American Express' financial advisors unit earned $157 million, up from $130 million a year ago, as managed assets increased and distribution fees grew mainly due to the record sale of mutual funds in the quarter, it said.
Sales of life and other insurance products and investment certificates also grew, but annuity sales declined.

Earnings from travel related services rose 10 percent to $315 million from $286 million. Revenues grew 7 percent mainly because a larger amount of purchases were charged on American Express charge and credit cards worldwide.
Total card billed business worldwide rose 15.3 percent to $47.9 billion for the quarter. Within the United States, card billed business rose 16.5 percent to $34.6 billion.

Billed business improved as the number of cards outstanding grew 8.3 percent to 41.9 million worldwide and each cardholder spent more, encouraged by rewards programmes and growing acceptance of the cards by merchants, it said.
Average basic cardmember spending rose 5.0 percent to $1,498 for the first three months of the year, Amex said.
Card usage also rose as the company launched new consumer and small business credit cards, as part of its strategy of building its lending portfolio through low- and no-fee cards.
"The travel-related services was healthy, credit quality was good and the financial advisors (business) reaccelerated somewhat," said Moshe Orenbuch, an analyst at Sanford C. Bernstein Co.
American Express stock rose $1.875 to $63.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
